metadata.description: 1-token liquidity provisioning helper for Coffer Pool

instructions.name: deposit_single_token
docs: Deprecated v5 ABI: always rejects before any token movement.

accounts.name: helper_lp_account

instructions.name: deposit_single_token_direct

instructions.name: deposit_single_token_planned
docs: V6 atomic zap with a curve-aware external allocation plan. The user's
old balances are protected and only the actual outputs of this call
fund the proportional join. Mint/epoch changes invalidate the quote.

instructions.name: withdraw_sol
docs: Recover lamports stranded on a pool's helper PDA.
There is no rent-exempt floor to respect here, and that is deliberate
rather than an oversight: the helper carries no data and is
System-owned, so a full drain simply reclaims the account, and its
address is re-derivable from `[HELPER_SEED, pool]` whenever it is
needed again. An earlier revision documented a rent-exempt guard that
the handler never applied — see `StldError::WouldBreakRentExempt`,
retained unraised for IDL numbering.
# Authority
Treasury PDA only — in practice via CPI from
`protocol_admin::stld_withdraw_sol`.
# Parameters
* `amount` — lamports; `> 0` and `<= source.lamports()`.

accounts.name: config
docs: Coffer-pool config whose `protocol_admin` is the authority for this
drain. In production it's the Treasury PDA of the `protocol-admin`
program.

accounts.name: pool
docs: The pool whose helper PDA is being drained. It is NOT merely a seed
source: it must belong to the config that authorised this call.
Without that binding, `config` and `pool` are independent inputs, and
the admin of config A could drain the helper of a pool governed by
config B — the helper PDA signs on nothing but its seeds, and those
seeds are derived from whichever pool the caller passes. That is the
same defect the audit raised as L-07 against coffer-pool's own
`withdraw_sol`, which binds `pool.config == config.key()`; this
instruction was rewritten for L-08 without picking the binding up.
It is latent only while one Treasury PDA governs every config. Rotation
is deliberately unpinned (L-09), so configs are expected to diverge.

accounts.name: source
docs: and dataless by construction; it signs its own outgoing transfer.

types.name: AssetConfig
docs: `CofferPool` v4 — per-pool state for a weighted AMM with virtual liquidity.
Storage layout: **Array-of-Structs (AoS)**. Per-token data lives in
`tokens: [TokenSlot; MAX_TOKENS]`. Each `TokenSlot` carries TWO nested
sub-structs:
- `config: AssetConfig`     — admin-controlled, rarely changes (mint,
token_program, weight, max_selloff, period).
- `dynamics: AssetDynamics` — auto-updated by user txs (balances,
protocol_fees_owed, sliding-window selloff state).
This mirrors Solend / MarginFi / Kamino's `Reserve { config, ... }`
pattern. Reading per-token data is a single struct lookup; auditors
see at a glance which fields a user can mutate vs which need pool
admin authority.
## Storage layout — DO NOT REORDER
Backends (`onchainPoolFetcher.ts`, indexer) read fields by raw offset.
Adding fields is OK if appended at the END (before the trailing
`reserved`) and `reserved` shrinks accordingly. Inserting in the
middle would require rewriting existing accounts.
## Derived (not stored) state
- `lp_mint`        — derived as `[LP_MINT_SEED, pool]` PDA.
- `lp_total_supply`— read from `lp_mint.supply` at runtime.
- `token_vaults[i]` — derived as ATA(pool, mint, tokens[i].config.token_program).
- `token_decimals`  — read from each mint account at runtime.

fields.name: mint
docs: Token mint pubkey for this slot. `Pubkey::default()` past `token_count`.

fields.name: token_program
docs: SPL Token or Token-2022 program ID for this token's vault/transfers.

fields.name: normalized_weight
docs: Normalised weight in basis points (sum across active slots == 10_000).

fields.name: max_selloff_pct
docs: Max cumulative sell volume of this token per sliding window,
expressed as a **percentage of the token's `virtual_balance`**
captured at window start, in units of `PERCENT_SCALE` (10_000 =
100%, so 1000 = 10%; resolution 0.01%). `0` disables the check for
this token. Must be `<= PERCENT_SCALE`. Set by pool_admin only.
The absolute cap for a window is `floor(max_selloff_pct *
vb_snapshot / PERCENT_SCALE)`, where `vb_snapshot` is
`AssetDynamics::selloff_vb_snapshot` (taken at window open). Using a
per-window snapshot — not the live `virtual_balance` — prevents an
in-window base-inflation bypass (see `math::max_selloff`).

fields.name: max_selloff_period_length
docs: Length of the sliding window in seconds. Ignored when
`max_selloff_pct == 0`. Set by pool_admin only.

fields.name: variable_fee_threshold_pct
docs: Variable sell-off **surge fee** curve (per token, `PERCENT_SCALE`
units; 10_000 = 100%). The fee rises as the token's max-selloff
window fills and is charged on `amount_out`, routed 100% to the
protocol bucket (`protocol_fees_owed`), never to LPs. See
`math::surge_fee`. The fee is active only when `max_selloff_pct > 0`
(it reads the window fill ratio) AND `fee_slope_high_pct > 0`.
Window fill ratio at which the surge fee starts (below it the fee is
0). E.g. 8000 = surge begins at 80% window fill.

fields.name: variable_fee_slope_low_pct
docs: Surge fee at the threshold (lower point of the curve).

fields.name: variable_fee_slope_high_pct
docs: Surge fee at ~100% window fill (upper point of the curve). Must be
`>= fee_slope_low_pct` and `<= PERCENT_SCALE`.

fields.name: is_active
docs: Per-token kill switch for the **input** side of swaps. When `false`,
swaps whose INPUT token is this one revert (`TokenInactive`); the
token can still be bought (as swap output) and liquidity ops are
unaffected. Defaults to `true` (active). Flipped by `set_token_active`
(pool-admin or protocol-admin/supervisor). Used to stop accepting a
compromised token without pausing the whole pool.

fields.name: variable_fee_slope_mid_pct
docs: Surge fee at the KINK — the middle of the three points that define the
curve. Between `variable_fee_threshold_pct` and this point the fee runs
linearly from `variable_fee_slope_low_pct` to here; beyond it, linearly
from here to `variable_fee_slope_high_pct` at full window fill.
This is the "target utilisation" shape lending protocols use (Evaa,
Aave, Compound): gentle while the window fills normally, steep once it
is nearly exhausted. Must satisfy
`slope_low <= slope_mid <= slope_high` — a fee that fell as the window
filled would invert the brake.

fields.name: variable_fee_kink_pct
docs: Window fill at which the curve kinks, in WHOLE PERCENT (0..=100), not
`PERCENT_SCALE` units — one byte is all that was left, and 1% is ample
resolution for a breakpoint.
`0` means "no kink": the curve degenerates to a single straight line
from `slope_low` at the threshold to `slope_high` at full fill, which
is what every pool written by the previous layout decodes as.
Must sit strictly between the threshold and full fill when set.

fields.name: virtual_balance
docs: Virtual balance (raw token units) used by the coffer invariant
math. Decoupled from `actual_balance` to enable concentrated
liquidity. Updated by swap / add_liquidity / remove_liquidity.

fields.name: actual_balance
docs: The LP-owned portion of this token's vault, in raw units.
It does NOT equal the vault's `amount`. The invariant is
`vault.amount == actual_balance + protocol_fees_owed`: protocol fees
sit in the same vault but are not LP capital, and `collect_protocol_fees`
pays them out without touching `actual_balance`. Sizing a withdrawal or
a deposit ratio against the raw vault balance would therefore hand LPs
the protocol's uncollected fees.
Reads of the vault should either use this field or subtract
`protocol_fees_owed` explicitly; the two are only equal on a pool whose
fees have just been collected.

fields.name: protocol_fees_owed
docs: Accumulated protocol fees for this token (raw units), awaiting
`collect_protocol_fees`. Stored separately from `actual_balance`
so LP value isn't diluted by uncollected fees.

fields.name: previous_selloff
docs: Sliding-window rate limiter: amount sold in the PREVIOUS window
(Cloudflare-style approximation, Solend RateLimiter pattern).

fields.name: current_selloff
docs: Amount sold in the CURRENT window.

fields.name: window_start_timestamp
docs: `Clock::unix_timestamp` when the current window started. Set to
`now()` at pool init.

fields.name: selloff_vb_snapshot
docs: Snapshot of this token's `virtual_balance` taken when the current
max-selloff window opened. The window's absolute cap is
`floor(config.max_selloff_pct * selloff_vb_snapshot / PERCENT_SCALE)`.
Snapshotting (rather than reading live `virtual_balance`) keeps the
cap un-inflatable within a window — selling raises the live vb, but
not this snapshot. `0` ⇒ uninitialised (re-captured on next check).

fields.name: config
docs: `CofferPoolConfig` this pool inherits governance from. Pinned at
init, used both as a PDA seed and at runtime in admin-instruction
constraints (`pool.config == config.key()`).

fields.name: bump
docs: Bump seed for the pool PDA. Stored so signer-seed reconstruction is
O(1) instead of an expensive `find_program_address` per CPI.

fields.name: token_count
docs: Number of active tokens in the pool, in [MIN_TOKENS, MAX_TOKENS] =
[2, 10]. Slots beyond `token_count` are zeroed and ignored.

fields.name: pool_id
docs: User-chosen 64-bit salt baked into the PDA seeds, allowing multiple
pools per config without re-deploying. Unique per (config, pool_id).

fields.name: swap_fee_rate
docs: Swap fee in hundredths of a basis point (precision
`SWAP_FEE_PRECISION` = 1_000_000). 100_000 = 10% (current cap).

fields.name: protocol_fee_rate
docs: Share of each swap fee taken by the protocol, in basis points
(precision `PROTOCOL_FEE_PRECISION` = 10_000). 5_000 = 50% (cap).

fields.name: created_at
docs: Pool creation `Clock::unix_timestamp`. Informational only.

fields.name: pool_enabled
docs: Master kill switch — when `false`, swaps and add/remove liquidity
all revert. Only `protocol_admin` can flip this.

fields.name: swaps_enabled
docs: Trading switch — `false` blocks swaps but still allows LP
add/remove. Either `pool_admin` or `config.protocol_admin` can flip.

fields.name: pool_admin
docs: Per-pool admin. Owns: rotate swap_fee_rate, toggle swaps_enabled,
set range_manager, set max_selloff, transfer/disable itself.

fields.name: pending_pool_admin
docs: Pending successor for `pool_admin` during a 2-step transfer.

fields.name: range_manager
docs: Pubkey allowed to call `range_manager_update`. `Pubkey::default()`
⇒ no manager set.

fields.name: range_manager_enabled
docs: `false` ⇒ all `range_manager_update` calls revert.

fields.name: range_manager_max_vb_change_pct
docs: Max per-update change to a token's `virtual_balance`, as a
percentage of its current value, in `PERCENT_SCALE` units
(10_000 = 100%; 500 = 5%). Enforced per token in
`range_manager_update`.

fields.name: range_manager_max_weight_change_pct
docs: Max per-update change to a token's `normalized_weight`, same
`PERCENT_SCALE` units.

fields.name: tokens
docs: All per-token state. Slot `i` is for the i-th token. Slots past
`token_count` are zero-initialised and ignored.

fields.name: lookup_table
docs: Per-pool Address Lookup Table address. Holds pool-scoped accounts
(pool PDA, LP mint, vaults, mints, token programs) so client SDKs
can build VersionedTransactions for `add_liquidity` / `remove_liquidity`
without hitting the 1232-byte legacy-tx ceiling on multi-token pools.
`Pubkey::default()` ⇒ ALT not yet initialised. SDK falls back to
legacy tx (will only work for small pools). Set by `initialize_pool_alt`,
frozen on-chain so depositors don't worry about authority abuse.

fields.name: _deprecated_banned_extensions
docs: Bytes 1651..1659 of the account. Until v6.1 this held the per-pool
`banned_extensions` Token-2022 policy bitmap snapshot. The policy was
removed in v6.1 (T19): the pool creator alone decides which mints go
into a pool and the frontend discloses the extensions they carry.
Mint admission is now purely structural
(`util::token::validate_mint_for_admission`).
Not trailing (it sits between `lookup_table` and
`range_manager_max_leverage_bps`), so it cannot be folded into
`reserved`. Existing pools still carry their old bitmap here; fresh
pools write `0`. No code path reads it. `migrate_to_v5` keeps its
`== 0` precondition on these bytes as part of the "untouched legacy
layout" proof (I-11). A later task may reuse these 8 bytes only
after an explicit migration instruction zeroes them — existing pools
hold non-zero values that would otherwise be misread.

fields.name: range_manager_max_leverage_bps
docs: Absolute ceiling on `virtual_balance / actual_balance` that the range
manager may leave a token at, in basis points (10_000 = 1.0×). `0`
disables the band.
The per-update percentage caps velocity, not distance: measured
against the live value each call, 5% steps compound to ~2.65× in 20
updates and ~131× in 100, so a manager — or a malfunctioning bot —
can walk the pool price arbitrarily far using only individually legal
moves. This band is the distance limit.
Anchored to `actual_balance` rather than to a captured snapshot on
purpose: real reserves only move when capital actually enters or
leaves, so the baseline cannot go stale the way a stored snapshot
does. Tokens with `actual_balance == 0` (sidelined) are exempt —
there is no real capital to anchor against.
Appended at the END (before `reserved`) per the layout rule above, so
every pre-existing field keeps its byte offset. Pre-upgrade pools
decode this as `0` (band disabled), which is the back-compatible
reading.

fields.name: range_manager_min_leverage_bps
docs: Lower half of the range manager's absolute envelope: the SMALLEST
`virtual_balance / actual_balance` ratio it may leave a token at, in
`PERCENT_SCALE` units. `0` disables the floor.
The ceiling alone was not an envelope. Output is priced off VIRTUAL
balances, so DEPRESSING a token's virtual balance makes the pool
believe it holds less than it does, and a sale into that token moves
the price far more than it should — the seller takes the other side's
real reserves at a fabricated rate. Fifty individually-legal 5% steps
took a 1M/1M pool's virtual balance down to ~77k in testing, after
which selling 100k returned ~565k instead of ~91k. Every step passed
the ceiling, because the ceiling only ever looks upward.
Checked on the same terms as the ceiling: only over the slots a call
actually writes, and skipped for sidelined tokens (`actual_balance ==
0`), which have no capital to anchor a ratio against.

fields.name: reserved
docs: Forward-compat padding for pool-level fields. Shrank 24 → 20 when
`range_manager_max_leverage_bps` was carved out of it, then 20 → 16 for
`range_manager_min_leverage_bps`, keeping `LEN` at the
mainnet-compatible 1683.

fields.name: protocol_admin
docs: Protocol-level admin. Allowed to: pause pools, change
`protocol_fee_rate`, collect protocol fees, drain via
`debug_withdraw_liquidity`, withdraw SOL from program-owned
accounts, and rotate itself via the
pending/accept flow. Set to a designated authority (typically the
Treasury PDA of the `protocol-admin` program) at config init.

fields.name: pending_protocol_admin
docs: Pending successor for `protocol_admin` during a 2-step transfer.
`Pubkey::default()` ⇒ no transfer in flight.

fields.name: default_protocol_fee_rate
docs: Default `protocol_fee_rate` (in basis points, max 5000 = 50%) seeded
onto every new pool created against this config. Pools may diverge
later via `set_protocol_fee_rate`.

fields.name: _deprecated_extension_policy
docs: Bytes 74..90 of the account (no discriminator offset: 66..82 of the
payload). Until v6.1 these held the `banned_extensions` /
`hard_banned_extensions` Token-2022 extension-policy bitmaps. The
policy was removed in v6.1 (T19): the pool admin alone decides which
mints go into a pool and the frontend discloses the extensions they
carry. Mint admission is now purely structural
(`util::token::validate_mint_for_admission`).
Existing configs still carry non-zero bytes here. No code path reads
them; they are not part of the zero-check that `reserved` is subject
to. A later task may reuse these 16 bytes only after an explicit
migration instruction zeroes them.

fields.name: reserved
docs: Forward-compatibility padding so future fields can be added without
migrating existing config accounts. Shrank 120 → 112 when the
(now deprecated) second policy bitmap was carved out of the tail.

types.name: SingleTokenDeposit
docs: Receipt of the retired v5 `deposit_single_token` route. Nothing emits it
any more (the route was removed under audit L-16); the declaration is
kept so indexers can still decode historic v5 logs from the IDL and so
the event list stays append-only.
# Fields
* `helper`                   — helper PDA pubkey.
* `pool`                     — Coffer Pool PDA.
* `user`                     — depositor.
* `token_in_index`           — index of the supplied token.
* `amount_in`                — raw input.
* `allocations`              — pre-CPI per-token slice plan.
* `deposited_amounts`        — post-CPI helper balances actually fed
to `add_liquidity` (after the v5 LP-ratio pre-cap).
* `lp_received`             — LP minted to the user.
* `dust_refunded`            — per-token refund helper → user, index
aligned with `allocations` / `deposited_amounts`. Previously a single
sum across every mint, which added raw amounts of different decimals
together and produced a number that meant nothing.

fields.name: dust_refunded
docs: Index-aligned with `allocations` / `deposited_amounts`. Summing raw
amounts across mints of different decimals — the previous `u64` —
is not a meaningful quantity.

types.name: SingleTokenDepositDirect
docs: Receipt for the direct route. `deposited_amounts` are measured actual
token debits of the join (after both crops); `dust_remaining` contains
only this zap's unspent budget, excluding all prior wallet balances.

types.name: StldSolWithdrawn
docs: Emitted by `withdraw_sol` after lamports move out of a stld-owned
account.
